newsitem.title: UK: Loyalist bomb found near Sinn Fein office.
newsitem.headline: Loyalist bomb found near Sinn Fein office.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland said on Sunday they had defused a bomb planted by pro-British Loyalists outside the Belfast offices of their ideological foes, the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein.
Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary, Sir Patrick Mayhew, also blamed the incident on Loyalists, who have officially been observing a ceasefire since October 1994.
The device was mounted in a car which was left near the offices of Sinn Fein, which seeks an end to British rule of Northern Ireland, in the New Lodge area of Belfast.
Loyalists, Protestants who pledge unswerving allegiance to British rule, called their truce to get their political spokesmen into Belfast peace talks.
The device was found as Irish republicans marked the 1916 Easter Rising against British rule in Ireland with parades and rallies across the island.
